question: A 23-year-old girl is referred by her obstetrician for the study of thrombocytopenia. Her platelets in the first prenatal evaluation a month ago were 42,000 / uL. She is 16 weeks pregnant and does not report hemorrhagic manifestations. Physical examination is normal. Hemogram: leukocytes 8,500 / uL, Hb 12 g / dL, platelets 51,000 / uL. The revision of the blood smear reveals platelets in accumulations. What is the diagnostic suspicion?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Platelets 42,000/uL in the first prenatal evaluation -> Platelets 51,000/uL in the current evaluation -> Platelets in accumulations on blood smear -> Diagnostic suspicion: Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy -> 80%
CHAIN: Platelets in accumulations on blood smear -> Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy -> Diagnostic suspicion: Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy -> 85%
enhanced_information: The diagnostic suspicion in this case is Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy. The presence of platelets in accumulations on the blood smear supports this suspicion. Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy is the most likely cause of the low platelet count in this pregnant patient without hemorrhagic manifestations.
analysis: Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy is the most likely diagnosis in this case based on the patient's presentation of low platelet count without hemorrhagic manifestations during pregnancy. The presence of platelets in accumulations on the blood smear further supports this suspicion. Thrombocytopenia of pregnancy is a common condition in pregnant women and is usually mild and asymptomatic.
